standard: The company should pay undisputed invoices within 30 calendar days after receiving a correct invoice and accepting the related work or service. The company may hold disputed amounts until the issue is resolved. Any late fee must not be more than 1% per month.

Either party should be able to end the agreement for convenience by giving 30 days written notice. For a normal contract breach, the party in breach should receive 10 business days to fix the problem before termination. Immediate termination may be allowed for fraud, serious security incidents, or illegal activity.

Personal data may be used only for the agreed purpose and only when necessary. Data must be encrypted while being sent and while being stored. The company must be told about a confirmed data breach within 48 hours. New subprocessors need prior approval. Personal data must be deleted or returned within 30 days after the service ends.

Both parties must protect each other's confidential information and use it only for the agreement. Public information, information already known, and independently developed information are excluded. The duty should continue for at least three years after the agreement ends. Trade secrets remain protected while they are legally considered trade secrets.

An automatic renewal period must not be longer than 12 months. The customer should not be required to give more than 30 days notice to stop renewal. A renewal reminder should be sent at least 45 days before the renewal date.

After payment, the customer should own custom work created specifically for the customer. The vendor keeps ownership of tools and materials created before the agreement. If the vendor's earlier materials are included in the work, the customer should receive a permanent licence to use those materials as part of the delivered work.

For ordinary contract claims, total liability should normally be limited to the fees paid during the previous 12 months. The limit should not apply to fraud, gross negligence, confidentiality breaches, data protection breaches, or intellectual property infringement.
